input.content:
# Strategy — chosen 16 November 2026

## The reasoning

Morgan's assets: evenings and weekends, strong writing, workable Python,
up to $2,000 of savings, one volunteer analyst (~5 h/week), and a growing
local network. That rules out original technical alignment research at the
frontier, and the newsletter space is crowded.

What one careful part-time person *can* do better than almost anyone:
**patient, well-sourced accountability work that nobody owns.**

## The project: Frontier Commitments Tracker

Frontier AI labs make public safety commitments constantly — in responsible
scaling policies, summit pledges, testimony, blog posts, model cards. Nobody
systematically records them, tracks when they are quietly revised or
dropped, or checks whether observable behaviour matches them. Journalists,
grantmakers, and regulators each rediscover fragments of this from scratch.

Halcyon Threshold will maintain:

1. **A dataset** of discrete, citable commitments (who, what, when, source,
   precision, verifiability, status), kept in this repository with full
   provenance.
2. **Status assessments** on a conservative methodology: a commitment is
   only marked "kept", "revised", "lapsed", or "unverifiable" with linked
   evidence; we never speculate.
3. **A quarterly written report** summarising changes — the publishable
   artifact, suitable for Alignment Commons and for citation in regulatory
   processes (e.g. incident-reporting dockets).

Why this is the right fit:
- **Neglected**: no maintained public resource does this.
- **Tractable**: it's reading, structuring, and writing — Morgan's strengths;
  the data work fits Priya's offer exactly.
- **Compounding**: value grows with every month of maintenance; a lone
  part-timer's consistency is the moat.
- **Robustly good**: useful whether the future needs faster regulation,
  better lab norms, or just an honest historical record. It informs rather
  than campaigns, which also keeps Halcyon Threshold credible.

## Funding

- Emberfall rapid grant (draft in `grants/`): $12,000 to buy Morgan time and
  cover analyst contracting + tools. Closes 30 Nov.
- Compute needs are trivial; Compute Commons credits only if we later add
  automated monitoring.
- Morgan's own money: reserve the $2,000 for domain/hosting/incidentals only.

## What we deliberately do NOT do

- No campaigning, petitions, or hot takes — credibility is the asset.
- No "AGI consulting" or punditry.
- No growth-for-growth's-sake (newsletter, merch, community Discord) until
  the tracker has a v1 and a first quarterly report.

## 90-day milestones

1. **By 30 Nov**: grant submitted; schema agreed with Priya; 25 seed
   commitments entered.
2. **By 31 Dec**: 100+ commitments, methodology page, website live
   (post-HR-clearance), tracker repo public.
3. **By 15 Feb**: first quarterly report published and submitted to
   Alignment Commons.

# Frontier Commitments Tracker — data schema (v0.1 draft)

One row per discrete commitment. Proposed fields (to be refined with Priya):

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| id | Stable id, e.g. `2026-001` |
| org | Lab/company making the commitment |
| date_made | Date the commitment was made public |
| source_url | Primary source (archive link preferred) |
| source_type | RSP / summit pledge / testimony / blog / model card / interview |
| text_exact | Verbatim quote of the commitment |
| summary | One-line neutral paraphrase |
| precision | binding-specific / specific / vague-aspirational |
| verifiable | externally-verifiable / partially / not-verifiable |
| trigger | What condition/date makes it checkable |
| status | active / kept / revised / lapsed / unverifiable |
| status_evidence_url | Evidence for the current status |
| last_reviewed | Date of last review |
| notes | Caveats, context |

## Method rules (v0.1)

1. Primary sources only; archive every source at time of entry.
2. `text_exact` is sacred — no paraphrase in that field, ever.
3. Status changes require linked evidence and a dated note.
4. When in doubt, "unverifiable" — we never infer violations.
5. Every entry reviewed by a second person before the status is published.

## Seed sources to mine first

- Published responsible scaling / preparedness / frontier safety policies
- International AI summit commitments (2023–2026)
- Legislative testimony by lab leadership
- Model cards and system cards for frontier releases

# Emberfall Fund — Rapid Grant Proposal (DRAFT for Morgan's review)

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold (morgan@halcyonthreshold.org)
**Amount requested:** $12,000
**Duration:** 4 months (December 2026 – March 2027)
**Deadline:** 30 November 2026. *Morgan must review and submit personally —
Emberfall requires the named applicant to be the accountable person.*

## What we will do

Frontier AI labs make public safety commitments continually — in responsible
scaling policies, summit pledges, testimony, and model/system cards. No one
maintains a public record of what was promised, when commitments are quietly
revised or dropped, or whether observable behaviour matches them.
Journalists, grantmakers, and regulators each reconstruct fragments of this
from scratch, and weak or abandoned commitments face no memory.

Halcyon Threshold will build and maintain the **Frontier Commitments
Tracker**:

1. **A public dataset** of discrete, citable commitments (verbatim text,
   primary source, archived link, precision, verifiability, trigger
   condition, status), with full provenance in an open repository.
2. **A conservative status methodology**: entries are marked kept / revised /
   lapsed / unverifiable only with linked evidence; we never infer
   violations. Every published status is reviewed by a second person.
3. **A quarterly report** summarising changes, written for journalists,
   funders, and regulators, and submitted to community venues (e.g.
   Alignment Commons) and relevant dockets.

the major frontier labs and the 2023–2026 summit pledges), published
methodology, public website, and the first quarterly report (by 15 February

analyst (~5 h/week) is designing the dataset schema. The project is
deliberately scoped to be sustainable for a small, consistent team:
the moat is patience and rigor, not scale.

This work is robustly useful across futures: it supports better lab norms,
informs regulation (e.g. incident-reporting rules), and creates an honest
historical record — while remaining non-campaigning, which protects its
credibility and citability.

with 150+ sourced entries; first quarterly report published by 15 February

submission) by end of grant. Morgan Hale is solely accountable for delivery.

# Public comment — docket FMIR-2026-0042 (Frontier Model Incident Reporting)

**STATUS: DRAFT — DO NOT FILE until Morgan confirms HR clearance.**
Comments are published with the filer's name. Deadline: **20 November 2026**
via https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042
If HR clearance has not happened by 19 November, we skip this round.

---

Re: Proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule, docket FMIR-2026-0042

I write in support of the proposed rule, with three suggestions from the
perspective of an independent project that tracks the public safety
commitments of frontier AI developers.

**1. Require incident reports to reference the developer's own published
safety policies.** Frontier developers have published responsible scaling
and preparedness policies that specify thresholds and responses. Reports
filed under this rule should state which internal policy provisions, if
any, the incident implicated and whether the specified response occurred.
This costs developers little — the policies are their own — and transforms
reports from isolated anecdotes into checkable records.

**2. Publish a public, machine-readable index of reports.** Even where
report contents are legitimately confidential, the existence, date,
developer, and category of each incident should be public in a structured
format. Independent researchers and journalists cannot provide the
accountability this rule intends if the record itself is invisible.

**3. Define "incident" to include commitment-triggering events, not only
harms.** A near-miss that crossed a developer's own declared capability or
safety threshold is precisely the event this rule should surface, whether
or not downstream harm occurred.

Public commitments without a public record of performance do not build the
trust this moment requires. This rule can supply the record. I urge its
adoption with the strengthened transparency provisions above.

Respectfully submitted,
Morgan Hale
Founder, Halcyon Threshold

Halcyon Threshold

A public record of what frontier AI labs promise — and what happens next.

Why

The arrival of very capable AI systems may be the most consequential event of our lifetimes. The organisations building them make public safety commitments constantly — in scaling policies, summit pledges, testimony, and model cards. Yet no one maintains a careful public record of what was promised, when commitments are quietly revised, or whether behaviour matches words. Memory is a public good. We're building it.

What we do

The Frontier Commitments Tracker is an open, fully sourced dataset of discrete safety commitments by frontier AI developers, maintained under a conservative methodology: every entry quotes its primary source verbatim, every status change requires linked evidence, and we never infer violations. What we don't do

No campaigns, no petitions, no punditry. The tracker is useful to journalists, researchers, funders, and regulators precisely because it only says what can be shown.

Get involved

We welcome careful readers, data-minded volunteers, and corrections — especially corrections. Write to morgan@halcyonthreshold.org.

Halcyon Threshold · 2026
